incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan (R.O.C.) Company Act, Articles 2, 98, 101, 108, 113, 387 and 393; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 7, 8, 10 and 12; and, where the direct shareholder is a Mainland China enterprise, Articles 72 and 73 of the Statute Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, together with the Regulations Governing Permission for Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Persons or Companies; plus the Company Registration Rules of the Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Section; Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs for shareholder approval; municipal government for business registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation and Registration of a Limited Company, together with the Articles of Incorporation, Investment Approval Letter and Company Name Pre-Approval Certificate, submitted through the MOEA Company Registration One-Stop Online Application System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Taiwan Company Act. However, the Investment Commission requires foreign or Mainland China shareholders to remit the full subscribed capital into a blocked escrow account with an authorized foreign exchange bank in Taiwan; the bank and a CPA verify the remittance before incorporation registration, and the funds remain blocked until the Company Registration Certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the undersigned initial directors of [CN WFOE LTD] (the Company), acting as the first board of directors (or, in the event the Company is formed with a single statutory director, by that sole director acting in accordance with Article 108 of the Taiwan Company Act), that the incorporation of the Company under the laws of Taiwan, as a limited liability company wholly owned by the foreign investor, be and hereby is ratified, approved, and confirmed in all respects. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the authorized share capital of the Company shall be the amount set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, and that the subscriber agrees to subscribe for all issued capital in consideration for the contribution of cash, such subscription to be paid into a blocked escrow account in Taiwan designated for investment approval verification, and that no capital contribution shall be deemed made unless fully paid and verified by a certified public accountant. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [address] in Taiwan, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and the directors are authorized to execute the lease or rental agreement, pay rent, and register such office with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are appointed as statutory officers of the Company: [Name] as General Manager and lawful representative for daily operations; [Name] as Chief Financial Officer and responsible person for tax filings; and [Name] as Compliance Officer with responsibility for the Company's anti-money-laundering and investment reporting obligations, effective immediately and continuing until removal or resignation by a subsequent resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank] is designated as the Company's principal banking institution, and the bank is authorized to open corporate accounts, maintain blocked escrow accounts, accept inward remittances, issue letters of credit, and honor instructions from any two of the above-named officers under a dual-signature authority matrix. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to prepare, execute, notarize, and file all incorporation documents, articles, declarations, and other instruments, and to pay all fees, required for the registration of the Company with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the Investment Commission. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all actions taken by the directors and officers prior to the date hereof in connection with the Company's incorporation are ratified and confirmed. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned directors have executed this resolution in the City of Taipei, Taiwan, on this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Investment Approval and Company Name Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs for foreign or Mainland China shareholder approval; Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs for company name and business scope pre-approval via the MOEA Company Registration One-Stop Online Application System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the investment application in Chinese or bilingual format, execute a power of attorney in favor of a Taiwan resident agent, and state the proposed business scope as passive holding of shares, collection of dividends, and management of subsidiary equity. If the ultimate investor is from Mainland China, file under the Mainland Investment approval track and respond to any negative-list or national-security queries. After the Investment Commission issues the approval letter, apply to the Department of Commercial Affairs for company name and business scope pre-approval. Select three alternative names in Chinese and English to avoid rejection; the name reservation is valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Investment application form with beneficial owner declaration
Notarized Power of Attorney for local agent
Parent company certificate of incorporation, articles of association, and board resolution
Audited financial statements or bank reference for funding source
Proposed Articles of Incorporation and business scope statement
Company name pre-approval application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query or conditional approval, respond in writing within 30 days or submit an amended investment plan with the required authentication. If the company name pre-approval is rejected due to confusion with an existing name, file a new application selecting alternate names; any refusal may be administratively appealed to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance to Blocked Escrow and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank in Taiwan, supervised by the Central Bank of Taiwan and the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the original investment approval letter to the chosen authorized foreign exchange bank and open a blocked investment escrow account in the name of the proposed company or the investor pending incorporation. Instruct the parent company to remit the subscribed capital by SWIFT using the approval case number as the remittance reference. The bank will report the remittance to the Central Bank and issue a foreign exchange remittance certificate. The funds must remain blocked until the company registration certificate is issued and the CPA capital verification report is completed. If funds are designated with the wrong reference or are subject to AML screening, provide the corporate chart and source-of-funds evidence.
required_dossiers: Investment approval letter
Application to open a blocked investment escrow account
KYC forms and corporate registers of the investor
Passport or business license of the investor
SWIFT remittance instructions and source of funds declaration
Draft Articles of Incorporation for bank reference
Registered office address commitment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application due to KYC or AML concerns, provide a group structure chart, evidence of legality of funds, and a notarized undertaking; alternatively transfer the application to another authorized foreign exchange bank. If the Central Bank queries the remittance, file an exchange declaration correction through the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, Notarization and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan District Court Notary Office or licensed Taiwan Notary Public; independent certified public accountant registered under the Business Entity Accounting Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the capital remittance is confirmed, convene the shareholders and the initial directors to execute the Articles of Incorporation, the director consent forms, and the statutory officer appointment forms. The Articles must state the company name, registered office, business scope, capital structure, and governance matters. Notarize the signatures before a Taiwan district court notary or licensed notary. Engage an independent Taiwan CPA to verify the bank escrow balance and issue the capital verification report. The CPA report must be dated after the escrow remittance and must reconcile the subscribed capital with the bank certificate; this report is indispensable for MOEA registration.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation
Shareholder resolution of the parent company
Notarized director and officer consent forms
Bank foreign exchange remittance certificate and escrow statement
CPA capital verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or CPA requires declarations or amendments, correct the documents and re-execute with original signatures. If the CPA refuses to certify because invested capital is inconsistent, procure supplementary remittance or amend the capital amount by a new shareholder resolution and reapply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Section via the Company Registration One-Stop Online System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application to the MOEA Department of Commercial Affairs through the Company Registration One-Stop Online System. Attach the name pre-approval certificate, Investment Commission approval letter, notarized Articles, CPA capital verification report, bank escrow certificate, registered office lease or landlord consent with building use permit, and identification documents of all directors and officers. MOEA will examine the legality of the business scope, the validity of the capital, and compliance with foreign or Mainland investment conditions. Upon approval, MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate and company unification number. The company comes into existence at this point, and the escrow funds may be released to the company operating account.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form
Name and business scope pre-approval certificate
Investment Commission approval letter
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
CPA capital verification report
Bank escrow certificate
Registered office lease contract or landlord consent with building use permit
Identification and consent forms for directors and statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a deficiency notice, respond within 15 days through the same portal with the requested corrected documents. If the application is suspended because the registered office or business scope is defective, update the consent or narrow the scope by revised Articles. A formal refusal can be challenged by administrative appeal before the Executive Yuan within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Business, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; municipal government business registration office; Bureau of Labor Insurance, Ministry of Labor if employees are hired.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the company registration certificate is obtained, register the company with the local National Taxation Bureau for corporate income tax and business tax. Apply to the municipal government for business license registration if required by local regulations, and apply for uniform invoice registration with the tax authorities. Even a passive holding company must file annual returns and declare dividends; therefore obtain the corporate seal specimen and register the statutory bank signatories. Register with the Bureau of Labor Insurance only upon hiring employees. Maintain digital and paper corporate records for tax authority inspection.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate
Business tax and uniform invoice registration application
Corporate seal specimen and responsible person identification
Registered office lease or use permit
Bank account certificate and authorized signatory form
Articles of Incorporation and shareholder resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau rejects the uniform invoice registration because the registered office is not suitable, submit the building use permit and landlord consent; if the municipal government questions the use of the premises, provide a certified office-use statement. Late registrations may apply for administrative leniency before penalty is assessed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6420 passive equity holding; no industrial authority clearance required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license required under industrial and physical licensing regimes; the company only needs tax registration and uniform invoice registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt under the Taiwan Environmental Impact Assessment Act; this passive equity holding SPV has no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations and does not meet any threshold for an Environmental Impact Assessment report or environmental registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No quantitative thresholds applicable; no wastewater discharge, no VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste generation. The only compliance is ordinary office waste disposal under municipal waste management rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No Civil Defense permit or industrial fire safety approval required for an office-only holding company; the registered office must comply with the Taiwan Fire Services Act for general commercial buildings and the Occupational Safety and Health Act for office workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, operating the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) online portal at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CN WFOE, as a resident limited liability company, obtains its unified social credit code (USCC) automatically issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) upon incorporation; the USCC serves as the taxpayer identification number (TIN) and VAT registration number. Tax registration is completed through the e-Tax portal by logging in with the USCC and submitting the basic registration data within 30 calendar days after business licence issuance. For a foreign non-resident corporate shareholder (e.g., the Taiwanese parent) that derives China-source dividends or interest, the withholding agent must apply for a non-resident TIN with the competent tax authority by submitting the foreign incorporation certificate, a valid Certificate of Tax Residence, and the underlying payment documentation; upon approval, the authority issues a non-resident taxpayer identification number used exclusively for withholding filing and treaty benefit claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law; China does not provide a check-the-box election. The WFOE is statutorily taxed as a resident enterprise. Elective special tax treatment for tax-neutral corporate reorganisations and elective tax treaty benefit applications may be available via the competent tax authority, subject to documentary and substantive tests.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Annual taxable turnover exceeding RMB 5,000,000 (CNY 5 million) triggers mandatory registration as a general VAT taxpayer; below this threshold, the entity may remain a small-scale taxpayer with simplified levy rates. All entities must still complete income tax registration regardless of VAT scale.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China has mandated fully digital electronic invoices (all-electronic invoices, also known as full digital e-invoices) issued through the nationwide e-Tax invoicing platform. Invoices must be uploaded in real time for centralised fiscal clearance and authentication; the system assigns a unique invoice number and applies an anti-fraud digital stamp before issuance. System-to-system integration via tax authority APIs is mandatory for high-volume issuers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods qualifies for 0% VAT when the goods are physically exported from China, the exporter has completed customs clearance and obtained the customs export declaration, and the export proceeds are received and repatriated in foreign currency within the statutory period, with all supporting documents retained for verification. Qualifying cross-border services (including international transportation, R&D, software, and certain consulting services) supplied to overseas recipients are zero-rated or VAT-exempt provided the recipient is offshore, payment is made in foreign exchange, and the service is wholly performed outside China. Pure equity holding activities are outside the VAT scope and thus do not independently trigger zero-rating.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to ex-post audit and joint supervision by the STA and customs authorities. If the zero-rated or rebate claim is determined to be fraudulent, unverified, or not substantiated by the required customs and foreign-exchange paperwork, the tax authority will claw back all VAT refunded, impose late payment surcharge, and assess an administrative monetary penalty of between one and five times the false rebate amount under the Law on the Administration of Tax Levy and Collection; criminal liability may also arise under the Criminal Law for export-rebate fraud. Supporting documentation must be retained for at least five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, exercising the delegated foreign exchange administration authority of the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed but not fully liberalized foreign exchange control regime. The RMB is convertible on current account for trade, services, dividends, and legitimate distributions, but capital account inflows and outflows remain subject to registration, approval, quota, and negative-list controls. For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise used as a passive equity holding SPV, inbound equity capital must be routed through the SAFE FDI registration framework and can only be settled in RMB after a designated bank verifies the underlying capital contribution, negative-list compliance, and enterprise status. Despite nominal RMB convertibility, de facto restrictions appear at the point of cross-border remittance: capital account income cannot be used for activities outside the approved business scope or for speculative investments, and any change in capital purpose requires SAFE registration. Profit remittance to the Taiwan shareholder is treated as a current-account item after tax, so the bank will require audited financials, tax clearance certificates, dividend resolution, and evidence that the funds are genuine post-tax profits; delays or rejections occur when the passive holding structure lacks commercial substance, historical filings, or clean source-of-funds proof. The overall assessment is restricted current-account convertibility plus controlled capital-account access, with high documentary rigidity and strong bank-level KYC discretion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Administration rules, export proceeds must be repatriated into mainland China and logged in the bank's SAFE electronic trade monitoring system within the applicable trade-receipt deadline, generally no later than 90 days from the export customs declaration date for standard open-account exports unless a SAFE-registered deferred collection or offshore retention approval is obtained. There is no mandatory conversion ratio in the current current-account regime: the exporting WFOE may retain 100% of export receipts in a foreign currency account or convert voluntarily at the onshore spot rate, but every receipt must be matched to a customs/foreign exchange declaration and supported by contracts, invoices, customs declarations, and logistics records.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Not Viable (0/10). Offshore digital fintech EMIs and neobanks are legally barred from serving as the primary treasury or clearing bank for a mainland China WFOE. Under PBOC and SAFE licensing requirements, only domestic designated foreign-exchange banks and licensed RMB clearing banks may open corporate accounts, receive FDI capital, process cross-border wires, and convert RMB for the WFOE. An offshore EMI does not hold a SAFE foreign exchange settlement license and cannot clear SWIFT MT103 payments into the SAFE monitoring system; attempting to route capital or dividends through an EMI would create an unlicensed cross-border payment channel, trigger KYC red flags, and expose the structure to penalties. EMIs may only serve as a low-value notification or card issuer where there is a licensed domestic sponsor bank, but they cannot replace the Tier-1 commercial bank relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative of the WFOE, or a board-designated signatory holding an original power of attorney and board resolution, must appear physically at a designated domestic branch for the account-opening interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by Tier-1 banks in mainland China for a WFOE corporate bank account. The bank must verify the original business license, official company seal/chop, shareholder structure, and personal identity documents in person. Some banks permit an initial remote documentary pre-review, but final face-to-face KYC, interview, and seal card registration require physical presence in-branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented or opaque beneficial ownership chain across Taiwan and intermediate offshore holding companies, preventing the bank from identifying the ultimate natural-person controllers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified company registry extracts with apostilles or legalization for every entity in the ownership chain, group organizational chart, certified passports or national ID documents for all natural persons with 25% or more shareholding, audited financial statements for the direct and ultimate shareholders for the last three years, tax residency certificates, TINs, and a bank reference letter from each shareholder's existing banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial equity injection that appears inconsistent with a passive equity holding SPV and may suggest money laundering, unlicensed lending, or third-party financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth file including audited shareholder financials, shareholder dividend declarations, signed board resolutions approving the capital contribution, share purchase or loan agreements, bank statements showing the funds traceable from the ultimate investor's account, SWIFT instruction naming the direct remitter, and an explicit declaration confirming that no third-party funding or round-tripping is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Passive SPV with no local employees, no physical office, no tax filings, and broad holding purpose that triggers substance risk under Chinese anti-money laundering and tax rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance file consisting of a group organizational chart, local office lease agreement, payroll and social insurance contribution records if applicable, board minutes approving the passive holding scope, a 12-month transaction flow forecast, an undertaking not to conduct unlicensed financial business, historical PRC tax filings, and an economic substance memorandum explaining the commercial reason for the SPV.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border dividend outflows and future capital transfers to Taiwan creating heightened sanctions, cross-strait regulatory, tax leakage, and China banking scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax legal opinion confirming the China-Taiwan investment framework and withholding treatment, PRC corporate income tax withholding certificates, audited financial statements supporting distributable profits, dividend declaration board minutes, current-account transaction documentation, CRS and FATCA declarations for all account holders and BOs, and a compliance certification confirming that no sanctioned party is involved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan shareholder must remit the subscribed equity consideration directly from its own bank account to the WFOE's designated FDI capital account using SWIFT MT103, with remittance information referencing 'Equity capital injection to CN_WFOE_LTD under the approved investment contract and board resolution'. The receiving Chinese bank validates the SAFE FDI registration code, investment contract, and negative-list classification; then the proceeds are booked using the foreign exchange payment purpose code for capital contribution to a foreign-invested enterprise. After settlement, an independent Chinese CPA performs capital verification and issues a capital verification report. The funds may then be converted into RMB only for approved purposes within the WFOE's passive equity holding scope; any onward equity subscription to subsidiaries must be supported by subsidiary board resolutions, valuation or subscription agreements, and applicable SAFE records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The holding SPV should route outbound disbursements through the same domestic designated bank using SWIFT MT103 for clear cash payments, especially for service fees, administrative expenses, and equity subscriptions. For goods-related settlements, Commercial Letters of Credit can be advised through MT700 or MT710 where the bank provides payment undertaking against conforming documents. Documentary Collections under URC522 may be used for lower-risk trade settlements where the bank acts only as an intermediary and does not provide financing. Every outbound disbursement must be supported by contracts, invoices, tax documents, customs declarations, and, where required, SAFE registrations for foreign debt or capital outflows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY forward contracts executed with a designated bank, supported by genuine current-account or FDI-related cash-flow exposure
Onshore FX swaps between CNY and USD for working capital and dividend remittance timing management, with terms aligned to the actual underlying cash flows
Plain-vanilla CNY/USD option strategies purchased from a domestic designated bank for hedging only, not for speculative open positions
Cross-currency swaps permitted only where they hedge an approved external debt or shareholder loan flow with physical exchange of principal and interest

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible as onshore hedging for the WFOE; NDF trading is limited to offshore markets and is not recognized by SAFE for corporate risk management in mainland China

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Shareholders' Meeting, Financial Statements Adoption, and Profit Appropriation Resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed as a standalone return; meeting minutes retained at the registered office and distributed to shareholders; filed with the MOEA Administration of Commerce only where a director change, capital change, or constitutional amendment requires registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each fiscal year-end, in all cases no later than June 30 immediately following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual shareholders' meeting within the statutory window exposes responsible directors to competent-authority intervention, possible administrative fines under Company Act, and risk of judicial compulsory convening; continuing failure may be treated as refusal to comply with lawful authorities and can contribute to administrative strike-off or dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (CIT annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance – National Taxation Administration (Regional National Taxation Bureaus)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from May 1 to May 31 immediately following the applicable taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the return is not filed by May 31, the taxpayer is not regarded as having complied; after notification, a delinquency surcharge equal to 10% of the assessed tax is imposed, plus an additional 1% for every two days of late filing, capped at 10% of the assessed tax; a further delayed filing penalty may reach 20% of the assessed tax, with monthly postal-surplus interest on any unpaid tax; in extreme cases, the National Taxation Administration may deem taxable income by estimation and the responsible person may face personal liability for statutory penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Pre-Provision of Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax for the Current Year (Provisional CIT Payment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance – National Taxation Administration (Regional National Taxation Bureaus)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from September 1 to September 30, based on the prior fiscal year's assessed income tax liability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment or under-payment by September 30 accrues a late payment surcharge of 1% for every three days of delay, capped at 10% of the underpaid amount, plus interest at the prevailing postal savings rate; continuous non-payment may trigger a full tax levy and, if served and ignored, may lead to asset seizure and court-ordered enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder Register and Beneficial Owner (UBO) Electronic Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs – Administration of Commerce, through the national Company Registration e-Filing System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before March 31 of each year; the current required electronic filing window is January 1 to March 31, as officially notified by the competent authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Company Act Article 22-1, failure to file, late filing, or materially inaccurate filing is punishable by an administrative fine of NTD 50,000; the company will be ordered to rectify, and each successive failure to rectify attracts a further NTD 50,000 fine; additionally, false declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership may expose responsible persons to penalties under the Money Laundering Control Act, and repeated non-filing may lead to registration irregularities that can culminate in administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified Audited Financial Statements (triggered by statutory audit threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at the registered office for shareholders, creditors, and regulators; not an annual standalone filing unless requested by the tax authority or submitted with a major registration application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements must be completed and presented before the annual shareholders' meeting, and in practice must be finalised by May 31 to accompany the CIT settlement return if required or electively used
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the company crosses the statutory audit threshold and fails to have its financial statements independently audited and certified by a licensed CPA, the responsible person may be fined under the Business Entity Accounting Act; the tax authority may disregard the un-audited statements and compute taxable income on a deemed or estimated basis, and the company may lose the ability to evidence profit distributions or capital maintenance, exposing it to shareholder litigation and regulatory strike-off risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Continuity of Registered Office and Local Company Secretary / Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Administration of Commerce (via company registration records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous mandatory obligation; any change of registered office, agent, or principal place of business must be applied for within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a valid registered office in Taiwan means the company cannot lawfully receive official notices, service of process, or municipal correspondence; the competent authority may, after warning and a statutory grace period, issue an administrative order to dissolve or strike off the company under Company Act Article 10; the company may also be deemed non-operational and subject to deregistration procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20 and the applicable Ministry of Economic Affairs enforcement rules, a non-public limited company must have its financial statements audited and certified by a licensed independent CPA if: (1) paid-in capital exceeds NTD 30 million; OR (2) annual net operating revenue exceeds NTD 100 million; OR (3) the company is engaged in an industry requiring mandatory audit regardless of size (such as banking, insurance, securities, or other industries designated by the MOEA or FSC). A passive pure equity holding SPV that is below these thresholds and carries no operational revenue is generally exempt from the mandatory audit, but the National Taxation Administration may still request an audited report where the tax computation or compliance risk warrants deeper inspection, and lending or parent-group consolidation policies may require certification even in the absence of a statutory trigger.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For non-public Taiwanese companies, financial statements are prepared under the Business Entity Accounting Act, related Commercial Accounting Regulations, and the Enterprise Accounting Treatment Guidelines (commonly described as Taiwan SME GAAP); alternatively, the company may voluntarily adopt Taiwan-IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. A public company or any company listing securities would be required to apply Taiwan-IFRS. For the WFOE holding SPV, the applicable default framework is Taiwan SME GAAP, subject to the parent group electing IFRS for group consolidation purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 22-1, the company must annually file, through the MOEA electronic system, its complete shareholder ledger, director, supervisor, manager, and beneficial owner information between January 1 and March 31 (or the exact window announced by the MOEA). Any shareholding transfer must be reflected in the company's statutory shareholder register immediately; if the transfer causes a director, supervisor, manager, or 5%+ ultimate-beneficial-owner change, a formal amendment registration is required with the competent authority within 15 days of the event. The annual UBO confirmation is separate from the 15-day corporate registration rule and operates as an independent recurring compliance check, and the company must at all times keep a current register of beneficial owners available for inspection by the competent authority and AML enforcement units.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for a passive equity holding SPV; the WFOE is a Chinese tax resident, and only dividends received from a Chinese resident subsidiary are exempt under EIT Law Article 26(2). Preferential 15% high-tech/new-technology enterprise rates, R&D super-deduction, and free-zone tax holidays are unavailable to a pure equity holding vehicle lacking qualifying business activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, A Type) and applicable schedules, including A105000 for tax adjustments and A107011 for dividend exemption; filed electronically through the official e-Tax filing portal of the State Taxation Administration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly estimated CIT returns must be filed and paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the final annual Form A settlement must be filed and paid within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (May 31 for a calendar-year WFOE).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue (sales of goods, services, and other business revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A pure equity holding WFOE generally reports zero or de minimis operating revenue; any management fees charged to the Taiwan parent must be at arm's length and supported by contemporaneous economic analysis. Do not net intercompany service charges against shareholder costs.

Report direct costs of revenue-generating activities only. For an SPV, custodian bank charges and legal or administrative fees directly attributable to holding activities may be deductible; amounts incurred for the benefit of the Taiwan shareholder are not deductible and must be added back in Schedule A105000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, general and administrative expenses, and R&D expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include salary, rent, professional fees, and travel of WFOE directors and employees. For a shell SPV with no employees, excessive administrative fees paid to Taiwan affiliates are a transfer-pricing red flag; they must satisfy the benefit test and be substantiated by time sheets, project records, and arm's length fee evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses (interest, bank charges, exchange gains and losses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on intercompany loans is deductible only to the extent it is at arm's length and within the thin capitalization debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1 for non-financial enterprises under EIT Law Article 46 and Circular 2. Excess interest is not deductible and may be recharacterized as a dividend.

Distinguish domestic versus cross-border dividends. Dividends received from a Chinese resident subsidiary are tax-exempt and the exempt portion should be reported here and reversed out through Schedule A107011. Dividends received from the Taiwan operating subsidiary are taxable foreign-source income and must be included with foreign tax credit relief, not exempted.

Include gains or losses on disposal of subsidiary shares. Gains on disposal of Taiwan shares by the China-resident WFOE are taxable at 25%; creditable foreign taxes can be claimed only with source-country tax vouchers.

This is accounting profit before CIT. The SPV must reconcile accounting and tax bases. Dividends paid by the WFOE to the Taiwan shareholder are profit distributions, not deductible expenses, and cannot be included in cost or expense for tax purposes.

Complete Schedule A105000 for all adjustments. A pure holding SPV must add back non-deductible expenses, excessive interest, management fees without substance, and other arrangements lacking business purpose. If the WFOE is found to be a shell, a GAAR adjustment under Article 47 may be proposed to deny a portion of deductible costs.

A WFOE is entitled to carry forward tax losses for 5 years, but a holding company cannot deduct capital contributions or distributions. Only revenue-expense losses from holding activities are carried forward. The Taiwan parent cannot use the WFOE's losses to offset its own Taiwan tax because each is a separate taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and applicable tax rate (25%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable income must be positive if non-exempt investment income exists. The 25% headline rate applies; no 15% high-tech rate is available to a passive equity SPV. CIT at the WFOE level is separate from and prior to dividend WHT on distribution to Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable, foreign tax credits, quarterly prepayments, and final balance due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute annual tax after credits, offset quarterly estimated payments, and pay the balance by May 31. For the Taiwan shareholder, the WFOE must also file a withholding return and remit dividend WHT within 7 days of distribution; failure to do so creates a separate penalty charge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: RMB 2,000 per occurrence (up to RMB 10,000 for serious non-compliance) under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law; late payment: 0.05% daily interest surcharge under Article 32; understatement or evasion: 50%-500% of evaded tax under Article 63; withholding failures: 50%-300% of the unwithheld amount under Article 69; criminal fraud: referral under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, potential imprisonment up to seven years, public disclosure as a serious tax-violation case, credit blacklisting, and exit control.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid by the Chinese WFOE to a non-resident Taiwan enterprise shareholder under EIT Law Articles 3 and 37, unless reduced by an applicable arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Claim relief under the Cross-Strait Avoidance of Double Taxation Arrangement, where its implementing protocol is in force for the relevant year, by having the Taiwan shareholder provide a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate, a beneficial ownership declaration, proof of substantive business operations in Taiwan, and evidence that it directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE's capital for the reduced 5% dividend rate. The WFOE must file the non-resident withholding return and treaty benefit application with the Chinese tax administration before or at the time of distribution; if the reduced rate is not accepted, 10% must be withheld and a three-year refund or treaty relief claim may be made with complete documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on interest and royalties paid to non-resident enterprises is 10%. Under the Cross-Strait Arrangement the rate may be reduced to 7% for interest and 7% for royalties if the Taiwan recipient is the beneficial owner; however, interest paid by the WFOE to a Taiwan shareholder in excess of an arm's length amount is non-deductible and may be recharacterized as a dividend, causing an additional 10% WHT to apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required if related-party transactions in the tax year equal or exceed RMB 400 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 200 million for intangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for related services, or RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers. Master File: generally required when total related-party transactions reach RMB 1 billion or when the enterprise is selected by the tax administration for transfer-pricing monitoring. A pure equity holding SPV will usually be below these thresholds but must still report related-party information annually and maintain contemporaneous evidence of arm's length conduct and substance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the general anti-avoidance rule (EIT Law Article 47) and the Beneficial Owner Rules of State Administration of Taxation Announcement 2018 No. 9 require the WFOE to demonstrate business rationale, real management and decision-making, office space, employees, and Core Income-Generating Activities in China if it wishes to claim treaty benefits or avoid recharacterization. A passive equity SPV without economic substance cannot rely on the Cross-Strait reduced rate and is exposed to anti-shell-entity and GAAR adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through false CIT return / artificial shift of profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE files Form A with zero or nominal revenue, claims large deductible management, consulting, and interest payments to the Taiwan related party, and deliberately understates or omits taxable investment income, such as dividends from the Taiwan operating subsidiary or capital gains on share disposals, while the same costs are shifted to erode the Chinese tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41, 44, 47 and 48; Tax Collection and Administration Law Articles 32 and 63 apply: tax authorities may disregard arrangements without economic substance, make an upward transfer-pricing adjustment, impose 0.05% daily late-payment interest, and impose a penalty of 50%-500% of the underpaid tax. If the evaded amount reaches the criminal threshold, Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law applies and the entity is fined, with responsible directors subject to imprisonment up to seven years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false annual returns or approve the profit-shifting arrangement may be ordered to make civil restitution; the tax bureau may withhold company and personal taxpayer credit clearance, impose exit control (travel ban) under Article 44 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law, and invoke PRC Company Law Article 20 to pierce the limited liability veil if the corporate structure is used to evade tax and prejudice creditors, making directors personally jointly and severally liable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and remit dividend WHT on outbound distribution to Taiwan shareholder
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE declares a shareholder dividend or makes a deemed distribution to the Taiwan parent, but does not withhold the statutory 10% (or the treaty rate) and does not file the non-resident withholding return within seven days, instead wiring the net amount directly to Taipei without attention to the withholding obligation under EIT Law Articles 37-40.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 69 requires the withholding agent to be fined 50%-300% of the amount it failed to withhold, and Article 32 imposes 0.05% daily late-interest on the overdue tax; the tax authority will demand the unpaid WHT from the WFOE. Public disclosure as a serious tax violation triggers credit blacklisting, restricted government procurement, and exit control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, financial director, and actual controller who knowingly directed the non-withheld dividend are jointly obligated to compensate the corporate shortfall; the exit ban can be applied personally, and if the unpaid tax is substantial, criminal charges may be brought for tax evasion or misappropriation of state tax revenues.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Beneficial ownership fraud / treaty abuse under the Cross-Strait arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan shareholder is a mailbox company with no employees, no office, no revenue, and no decision-making power, and the WFOE nevertheless claims the reduced 5% dividend rate by submitting a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate and a false beneficial owner declaration, while the ultimate owner is outside Taiwan and the purpose of the structure is to obtain treaty relief that is not economically deserved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: State Administration of Taxation Announcement 2018 No. 9 (Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Identification) and EIT Law Article 47 authorize recharacterization and denial of treaty benefits; 10% (or the full statutory) WHT is collected with 0.05% daily interest and a penalty from 50%-500% of the underpayment; false declarations may additionally constitute tax fraud under PRC Criminal Law Article 201.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The substance failure, if combined with personal approval of false treaty claim documentation, exposes directors to personal civil liability for the extra tax, interest, and penalties, and to criminal liability for fraudulent tax avoidance; corporate veil piercing applies when the WFOE and Taiwan shareholder operate a sham corporate form with no legitimate commercial purpose, and the Chinese court may order personal asset attachment and travel restriction.
